purpose: Provide parent-scoped notifications, delivery preferences and governed support with reliable ticket submission/status follow-up. Screen-specific role: FAQ Search.
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent mutes every notification category they can (everything except the un-mutable safety-critical ones) → the inbox still functions normally for viewing any notifications that do arrive (the safety-critical ones, plus any the parent didn't fully mute), never breaking or hiding the inbox itself based on preference state.
2. A parent submits a ticket, then submits a second, related ticket on the same topic before the first is resolved → both tickets exist independently in their ticket history (no automatic merging), though a support agent may manually link/merge them on the admin side if appropriate — the parent always sees an accurate reflection of what they actually submitted.
3. A parent's Account Deletion grace period expires (cascade completes) while they have an open, unresolved "Account Deletion Cancellation" ticket → consistent with C.21's cascade-worker boundary logic, if the ticket/cancellation wasn't actioned by Support before the deadline, the cascade proceeds as scheduled; the ticket should then be updated to reflect this outcome rather than remaining ambiguously "open" forever.
4. A parent searches the FAQ for a topic with no matching content → a clear "no results, here's how to contact Support" fallback is shown, never a dead-end blank search result.
5. A parent's billing-failure notification is configured to de-prioritized delivery (e.g., email-only, push de-prioritized) → it still must actually arrive via that remaining enabled channel; "de-prioritized" never means "sometimes doesn't arrive at all" — it's a channel/ordering preference, not a delivery-reliability reduction.
6. A parent views the Notifications inbox while offline → renders from cache with a staleness indicator; marking-as-read actions taken offline queue and sync on reconnect, consistent with the platform's general offline-action pattern.
7. A parent's ticket category is "safety concern" but the actual content, on review, turns out to be a routine billing question → support agents can recategorize a ticket on the admin side without the parent needing to resubmit; the parent's ticket-status view reflects the corrected category and any resulting SLA change transparently.
8. Two co-guardians on different devices both submit feedback/tickets about the same underlying issue independently → each ticket is tracked separately (consistent with Edge Case 2's no-auto-merge default), with support agents responsible for recognizing and coordinating related tickets manually if warranted.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| FAQ search returns zero results | Clear "no results, contact Support" fallback (Edge Case 4) |
| Ticket submission fails (network) | Local draft preserved, retried, never silently lost |
| Notifications inbox fetch failure | Cached last-known list shown with a staleness indicator |
| Mark-as-read action fails (network) | Optimistic local update, queued for retry, never blocks further interaction |
| Safety-critical notification delivery channel itself fails (e.g., push token invalid) | Falls back to the next enabled channel (e.g., email) rather than silently failing to deliver at all |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero notifications yet (new account) → friendly "Nothing here yet" empty state.
- Zero ticket history yet → friendly "You haven't contacted Support yet — search our FAQ or reach out anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Notifications inbox / Support Center: skeleton list shimmer.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Notifications inbox renders from cache; FAQ search and ticket submission require connectivity, indicated clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies on the existing OS notification-permission state already governed by the platform's general notification infrastructure (B.17).

functional_requirements.requirement: Notifications (Parent) components: inbox list, read/unread state, filters by type (source: screen catalog).
Notifications (Parent) actions: mark read, open the related deep-linked screen (source: screen catalog).
**Safety alerts cannot be muted; marketing ones can** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — a hard, zero-exception rule on the category-preference model itself, not just a UI convention).

**Safety-critical notifications (deletion grace period, billing failure) cannot be fully disabled, only de-prioritized in delivery channel** (source: NoorHeroes Blueprint — restated as the precise mechanism: a parent may downgrade *how* a safety-critical notification reaches them — e.g., push de-prioritized in favor of email-only — but never opt out of receiving it through *some* channel entirely).

Support Center components: FAQ search, contact-support form, ticket status (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Components: Consent toggles, AI history, export request, support chat"; NoorHeroes Blueprint "Notifications (Parent) & Support — Components: Notification type toggles, quiet hours, FAQ search, contact-support form, ticket status").
Support Center actions: toggle notification categories, set quiet hours, submit support ticket, view ticket history (source: screen catalog "Actions").

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog — restated as the canonical async-job UX pattern this feature's "Privacy & Support" surface must implement for export/deletion-adjacent requests).

**Parent Account Deletion cancellation during the 7-day grace period routes through Support, never self-service** (cross-ref C.21 FR-8 step 7) — the Support Center's contact-form/ticket flow is the actual mechanism through which a parent initiates this specific cancellation request; this document's ticket-submission flow must support a distinctly-tagged "Account Deletion Cancellation" category that routes to the appropriate priority queue.

Support tickets support a defined category taxonomy (e.g., billing, technical issue, content concern, safety concern, account-deletion-cancellation, general) — each category may route to a different internal queue/SLA, with safety-concern and account-deletion-cancellation categories receiving expedited priority.

The FAQ search is content-governed (admin-authored, scholar-reviewed where Islamic-content-adjacent) — never an AI-freeform-generated answer presented as official guidance, consistent with the platform's general content-governance discipline applied here to support content specifically.

A parent's notification-category preferences and quiet-hours configuration here are the **parent-facing counterpart** of B.17's shared Policy Engine — this feature writes to the same `notification_preferences` table B.17's Policy Engine reads from, with `child_id` null for parent-scoped preference rows (cross-ref B.17 §4.1's shared schema).

Every notification in the inbox deep-links to its related screen using the same Deep Link Resolution Service specified in B.17 (full revalidation on open) — this feature does not implement a separate, weaker deep-link path for parent-facing notifications.

Source PRD_Documents/Parent Area In-App (19-26)/Feature_C25_Notifications_Parent_Support.md §1.18 row 11; §1.7; §2; §6; §13
Purpose: Provide parent-scoped notifications, delivery preferences and governed support with reliable ticket submission/status follow-up. Screen-specific role: Contact Support Form.
Fields: Verified category taxonomy; Subject; Details; Submit Ticket; Draft preservation
Action contract:
Select category → selected chip/state; require authoritative safety-concern and account-deletion-cancellation taxonomy
Subject/details input → local draft; submit validation messages require approved copy
Submit valid online draft → create ticket → Ticket Submitted Confirmation → Ticket History
Deletion-cancellation entry preselects category and expedited queue; creates ticket only, never cancels deletion directly
Failure/offline → preserve draft and offer retry/reconnect; no claimed ticket created
Cancel/back → Support Center/FAQ invoking route; draft-loss warning only if source requirements establish it
Urgent safety email external action requires verified address and parent gate; source missing address remains blocked
States:
Draft default/selected category
Subject/details validation; approved requiredness and limits unresolved
Online submitting → submitted confirmation
Failure/offline retains draft and offers retry
Deletion-cancellation pretagged expedited category
No direct deletion cancellation on submit

name: Ticket Submitted Confirmation
frame2_status: No independently verified equivalent for this screen; global style inspiration must not replace approved copy
purpose: Provide parent-scoped notifications, delivery preferences and governed support with reliable ticket submission/status follow-up. Screen-specific role: Ticket Submitted Confirmation.
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent mutes every notification category they can (everything except the un-mutable safety-critical ones) → the inbox still functions normally for viewing any notifications that do arrive (the safety-critical ones, plus any the parent didn't fully mute), never breaking or hiding the inbox itself based on preference state.
2. A parent submits a ticket, then submits a second, related ticket on the same topic before the first is resolved → both tickets exist independently in their ticket history (no automatic merging), though a support agent may manually link/merge them on the admin side if appropriate — the parent always sees an accurate reflection of what they actually submitted.
3. A parent's Account Deletion grace period expires (cascade completes) while they have an open, unresolved "Account Deletion Cancellation" ticket → consistent with C.21's cascade-worker boundary logic, if the ticket/cancellation wasn't actioned by Support before the deadline, the cascade proceeds as scheduled; the ticket should then be updated to reflect this outcome rather than remaining ambiguously "open" forever.
4. A parent searches the FAQ for a topic with no matching content → a clear "no results, here's how to contact Support" fallback is shown, never a dead-end blank search result.
5. A parent's billing-failure notification is configured to de-prioritized delivery (e.g., email-only, push de-prioritized) → it still must actually arrive via that remaining enabled channel; "de-prioritized" never means "sometimes doesn't arrive at all" — it's a channel/ordering preference, not a delivery-reliability reduction.
6. A parent views the Notifications inbox while offline → renders from cache with a staleness indicator; marking-as-read actions taken offline queue and sync on reconnect, consistent with the platform's general offline-action pattern.
7. A parent's ticket category is "safety concern" but the actual content, on review, turns out to be a routine billing question → support agents can recategorize a ticket on the admin side without the parent needing to resubmit; the parent's ticket-status view reflects the corrected category and any resulting SLA change transparently.
8. Two co-guardians on different devices both submit feedback/tickets about the same underlying issue independently → each ticket is tracked separately (consistent with Edge Case 2's no-auto-merge default), with support agents responsible for recognizing and coordinating related tickets manually if warranted.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| FAQ search returns zero results | Clear "no results, contact Support" fallback (Edge Case 4) |
| Ticket submission fails (network) | Local draft preserved, retried, never silently lost |
| Notifications inbox fetch failure | Cached last-known list shown with a staleness indicator |
| Mark-as-read action fails (network) | Optimistic local update, queued for retry, never blocks further interaction |
| Safety-critical notification delivery channel itself fails (e.g., push token invalid) | Falls back to the next enabled channel (e.g., email) rather than silently failing to deliver at all |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero notifications yet (new account) → friendly "Nothing here yet" empty state.
- Zero ticket history yet → friendly "You haven't contacted Support yet — search our FAQ or reach out anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Notifications inbox / Support Center: skeleton list shimmer.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Notifications inbox renders from cache; FAQ search and ticket submission require connectivity, indicated clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies on the existing OS notification-permission state already governed by the platform's general notification infrastructure (B.17).

functional_requirements.requirement: Notifications (Parent) components: inbox list, read/unread state, filters by type (source: screen catalog).
Notifications (Parent) actions: mark read, open the related deep-linked screen (source: screen catalog).
**Safety alerts cannot be muted; marketing ones can** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — a hard, zero-exception rule on the category-preference model itself, not just a UI convention).

**Safety-critical notifications (deletion grace period, billing failure) cannot be fully disabled, only de-prioritized in delivery channel** (source: NoorHeroes Blueprint — restated as the precise mechanism: a parent may downgrade *how* a safety-critical notification reaches them — e.g., push de-prioritized in favor of email-only — but never opt out of receiving it through *some* channel entirely).

Support Center components: FAQ search, contact-support form, ticket status (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Components: Consent toggles, AI history, export request, support chat"; NoorHeroes Blueprint "Notifications (Parent) & Support — Components: Notification type toggles, quiet hours, FAQ search, contact-support form, ticket status").
Support Center actions: toggle notification categories, set quiet hours, submit support ticket, view ticket history (source: screen catalog "Actions").

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog — restated as the canonical async-job UX pattern this feature's "Privacy & Support" surface must implement for export/deletion-adjacent requests).

**Parent Account Deletion cancellation during the 7-day grace period routes through Support, never self-service** (cross-ref C.21 FR-8 step 7) — the Support Center's contact-form/ticket flow is the actual mechanism through which a parent initiates this specific cancellation request; this document's ticket-submission flow must support a distinctly-tagged "Account Deletion Cancellation" category that routes to the appropriate priority queue.

Support tickets support a defined category taxonomy (e.g., billing, technical issue, content concern, safety concern, account-deletion-cancellation, general) — each category may route to a different internal queue/SLA, with safety-concern and account-deletion-cancellation categories receiving expedited priority.

The FAQ search is content-governed (admin-authored, scholar-reviewed where Islamic-content-adjacent) — never an AI-freeform-generated answer presented as official guidance, consistent with the platform's general content-governance discipline applied here to support content specifically.

A parent's notification-category preferences and quiet-hours configuration here are the **parent-facing counterpart** of B.17's shared Policy Engine — this feature writes to the same `notification_preferences` table B.17's Policy Engine reads from, with `child_id` null for parent-scoped preference rows (cross-ref B.17 §4.1's shared schema).

Every notification in the inbox deep-links to its related screen using the same Deep Link Resolution Service specified in B.17 (full revalidation on open) — this feature does not implement a separate, weaker deep-link path for parent-facing notifications.

edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent withdraws the marketing consent, then later wants to re-grant it (e.g., decides they do want promotional emails after all) → re-granting an optional consent is supported as a straightforward toggle-back-on action, creating a new consent-ledger entry (consistent with A.1's append-only, versioned consent-recording pattern) rather than attempting to "undelete" the prior withdrawal record.
2. A parent requests a data export, then immediately requests a second one before the first completes → the second request either queues behind the first or is recognized as a duplicate-in-progress request (returning the existing request's status rather than spawning a redundant parallel export job) — implementation may choose either approach, but the parent must never see two simultaneously-conflicting "your export is ready" notifications for what should be one logical export.
3. An AI interaction occurs for a child whose family later requests full account deletion, and the 7-day grace period elapses → the AI Interaction History records for that family are subject to the same cascade-deletion/legal-retention rules as all other family data (cross-ref C.21's cascade worker), not independently retained beyond what's legally required.
4. A parent's AI Interaction History query spans a period with zero AI interactions (e.g., AI was disabled for that child the whole time) → shows an explicit "No AI interactions in this period" state, consistent with C.22's established empty-state pattern for the same conceptual absence.
5. A parent revokes a device that is, at that exact moment, in the middle of an active data-export-status poll from that same device → the in-flight read request may complete (read-only, low-risk), but any subsequent request from that revoked device fails authentication immediately after, consistent with C.23's established device-revocation timing pattern.
6. A parent changes the family-level language preference while a specific child has their own individually-overridden display language (per B.16) → the child's own override is unaffected; this screen's language picker only affects the family/parent-level default and any child without their own override.
7. A data export request is made for a family with a very large amount of historical data (long-tenured, many children) → the export job may take longer; the async status model already accommodates this via its "preparing" state, with no different handling needed beyond what the async design already provides.
8. A parent attempts to view AI Interaction History for a child whose AI has always been disabled (never enabled) → shows a friendly empty state distinct from "no interactions this period" — something like "AI has been off for this child the entire time," reinforcing that the absence is by configuration, not a missing-data issue worth flagging as suspicious.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Data export request fails to start (backend issue) | Clear retry option, never a silent failure |
| Duplicate export request while one is in-progress | Recognized and deduplicated, or queued; never two conflicting "ready" states |
| Consent withdrawal attempted on a required consent | Routed to the account-deletion explanation rather than a toggle action |
| PIN reset / device revocation failure | Standard C.19 error handling reused, no separate error path |
| Logout attempted with unsynced downloads | Confirmation prompt required before proceeding (FR-4) |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero AI interactions ever (AI always disabled) → distinct "AI has been off the entire time" framing (Edge Case 8).
- Zero AI interactions in a selected period (AI enabled but unused) → "No AI interactions in this period" framing (Edge Case 4).
- Zero data-export history yet → friendly "Request your first export anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Settings/Privacy screens: skeleton list shimmer for Consent Log, AI Interaction History, device list.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Settings screens render last-cached data offline; export requests, consent withdrawal, PIN reset, and device revocation all require connectivity and indicate this clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies entirely on the existing step-up authentication gate (C.19).

functional_requirements.requirement: Settings/Privacy & Support components (canonical, source NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Settings screen): Security (PIN/biometric reset), devices list, consent log, AI controls per child (cross-ref/link only, configuration owned by C.23), language picker, export/delete account.

Settings actions: reset PIN, revoke device, review/withdraw consent, request export, request account deletion (cross-ref C.21 for the deletion flow itself — this screen's role is the entry point/link).

**Export and deletion require step-up authentication; deletion shows the 7-day grace period explicitly** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — restated; the deletion *experience* itself is C.21's, this screen only requires the same step-up before linking into it).

**Logout requires confirmation if any unsynced offline downloads exist** (source: screen catalog "Settings — Navigation Rules") — a data-loss-prevention courtesy check specific to the logout action on this screen.

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Navigation Rules") — the same `data_requests` record is queryable from both surfaces.

AI Interaction History entries are **redacted at write time, not just at read time** — `ai_interactions.input_redacted`/`output_redacted` are the only fields that ever exist for this data; there is no corresponding unredacted column anywhere in the schema for a later read-time filter to fail and leak (source §9.5 schema notes — a hard, structural guarantee, generalizing C.22's flags-only Safety Report into the fuller, still-safe, history view this screen offers).

Each AI Interaction History entry carries `model_version` and `policy_result` (e.g., allowed/blocked/redirected) alongside the redacted input/output summaries and an `expires_at` retention boundary — giving parents genuine context (what kind of interaction, what the system decided) without ever exposing a raw, re-identifiable transcript.

Consent Log entries are individually reviewable and, for optional consents (personalization, voice/AI, marketing — cross-ref A.1 FR-5's required-vs-optional distinction), individually withdrawable; **required consents (Terms, Privacy Policy, child-data-processing) cannot be withdrawn without triggering the broader account-deletion path**, since withdrawing a required consent is functionally equivalent to revoking the basis for the account's existence (cross-ref A.1's consent model, restated here as this screen's withdrawal-eligibility rule).

Withdrawing the AI/voice consent specifically here has the identical effect as toggling AI off via C.23's AI Permissions screen — this screen and C.23 read/write the **same** underlying settings field, never two independently-tracked values that could drift out of sync.

The language picker sets the app's display language; this is the same setting B.16's child-Profile language toggle exposes per-child — at the parent level, this screen sets the **default/family-level** language preference, distinct from (but consistent in mechanism with) a child's own individual override, if any.

PIN reset and device revocation on this screen reuse C.19's exact `ParentGateLauncher`/session-list mechanisms — this screen introduces no parallel PIN-storage or session-management implementation of its own.

Data export produces a structured, parent-readable export of the family's own data (consent history, child profiles' progress summaries, AI interaction history, billing history) — **never** including another family's data, and excluding raw biometric data (which never existed in exportable form to begin with, per A.1/C.19's zero-biometric-storage guarantee).

Settings actions: reset PIN, revoke device, review/withdraw consent, request export, request account deletion (cross-ref C.21 for the deletion flow itself — this screen's role is the entry point/link).

**Export and deletion require step-up authentication; deletion shows the 7-day grace period explicitly** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — restated; the deletion *experience* itself is C.21's, this screen only requires the same step-up before linking into it).

**Logout requires confirmation if any unsynced offline downloads exist** (source: screen catalog "Settings — Navigation Rules") — a data-loss-prevention courtesy check specific to the logout action on this screen.

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Navigation Rules") — the same `data_requests` record is queryable from both surfaces.

AI Interaction History entries are **redacted at write time, not just at read time** — `ai_interactions.input_redacted`/`output_redacted` are the only fields that ever exist for this data; there is no corresponding unredacted column anywhere in the schema for a later read-time filter to fail and leak (source §9.5 schema notes — a hard, structural guarantee, generalizing C.22's flags-only Safety Report into the fuller, still-safe, history view this screen offers).

Each AI Interaction History entry carries `model_version` and `policy_result` (e.g., allowed/blocked/redirected) alongside the redacted input/output summaries and an `expires_at` retention boundary — giving parents genuine context (what kind of interaction, what the system decided) without ever exposing a raw, re-identifiable transcript.

Consent Log entries are individually reviewable and, for optional consents (personalization, voice/AI, marketing — cross-ref A.1 FR-5's required-vs-optional distinction), individually withdrawable; **required consents (Terms, Privacy Policy, child-data-processing) cannot be withdrawn without triggering the broader account-deletion path**, since withdrawing a required consent is functionally equivalent to revoking the basis for the account's existence (cross-ref A.1's consent model, restated here as this screen's withdrawal-eligibility rule).

Withdrawing the AI/voice consent specifically here has the identical effect as toggling AI off via C.23's AI Permissions screen — this screen and C.23 read/write the **same** underlying settings field, never two independently-tracked values that could drift out of sync.

The language picker sets the app's display language; this is the same setting B.16's child-Profile language toggle exposes per-child — at the parent level, this screen sets the **default/family-level** language preference, distinct from (but consistent in mechanism with) a child's own individual override, if any.

PIN reset and device revocation on this screen reuse C.19's exact `ParentGateLauncher`/session-list mechanisms — this screen introduces no parallel PIN-storage or session-management implementation of its own.

Data export produces a structured, parent-readable export of the family's own data (consent history, child profiles' progress summaries, AI interaction history, billing history) — **never** including another family's data, and excluding raw biometric data (which never existed in exportable form to begin with, per A.1/C.19's zero-biometric-storage guarantee).

edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent withdraws the marketing consent, then later wants to re-grant it (e.g., decides they do want promotional emails after all) → re-granting an optional consent is supported as a straightforward toggle-back-on action, creating a new consent-ledger entry (consistent with A.1's append-only, versioned consent-recording pattern) rather than attempting to "undelete" the prior withdrawal record.
2. A parent requests a data export, then immediately requests a second one before the first completes → the second request either queues behind the first or is recognized as a duplicate-in-progress request (returning the existing request's status rather than spawning a redundant parallel export job) — implementation may choose either approach, but the parent must never see two simultaneously-conflicting "your export is ready" notifications for what should be one logical export.
3. An AI interaction occurs for a child whose family later requests full account deletion, and the 7-day grace period elapses → the AI Interaction History records for that family are subject to the same cascade-deletion/legal-retention rules as all other family data (cross-ref C.21's cascade worker), not independently retained beyond what's legally required.
4. A parent's AI Interaction History query spans a period with zero AI interactions (e.g., AI was disabled for that child the whole time) → shows an explicit "No AI interactions in this period" state, consistent with C.22's established empty-state pattern for the same conceptual absence.
5. A parent revokes a device that is, at that exact moment, in the middle of an active data-export-status poll from that same device → the in-flight read request may complete (read-only, low-risk), but any subsequent request from that revoked device fails authentication immediately after, consistent with C.23's established device-revocation timing pattern.
6. A parent changes the family-level language preference while a specific child has their own individually-overridden display language (per B.16) → the child's own override is unaffected; this screen's language picker only affects the family/parent-level default and any child without their own override.
7. A data export request is made for a family with a very large amount of historical data (long-tenured, many children) → the export job may take longer; the async status model already accommodates this via its "preparing" state, with no different handling needed beyond what the async design already provides.
8. A parent attempts to view AI Interaction History for a child whose AI has always been disabled (never enabled) → shows a friendly empty state distinct from "no interactions this period" — something like "AI has been off for this child the entire time," reinforcing that the absence is by configuration, not a missing-data issue worth flagging as suspicious.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Data export request fails to start (backend issue) | Clear retry option, never a silent failure |
| Duplicate export request while one is in-progress | Recognized and deduplicated, or queued; never two conflicting "ready" states |
| Consent withdrawal attempted on a required consent | Routed to the account-deletion explanation rather than a toggle action |
| PIN reset / device revocation failure | Standard C.19 error handling reused, no separate error path |
| Logout attempted with unsynced downloads | Confirmation prompt required before proceeding (FR-4) |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero AI interactions ever (AI always disabled) → distinct "AI has been off the entire time" framing (Edge Case 8).
- Zero AI interactions in a selected period (AI enabled but unused) → "No AI interactions in this period" framing (Edge Case 4).
- Zero data-export history yet → friendly "Request your first export anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Settings/Privacy screens: skeleton list shimmer for Consent Log, AI Interaction History, device list.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Settings screens render last-cached data offline; export requests, consent withdrawal, PIN reset, and device revocation all require connectivity and indicate this clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies entirely on the existing step-up authentication gate (C.19).

purpose: Give parents granular consent, safe AI-history, account security, language and asynchronous family data-rights controls. Screen-specific role: Consent Detail (full text + status).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent withdraws the marketing consent, then later wants to re-grant it (e.g., decides they do want promotional emails after all) → re-granting an optional consent is supported as a straightforward toggle-back-on action, creating a new consent-ledger entry (consistent with A.1's append-only, versioned consent-recording pattern) rather than attempting to "undelete" the prior withdrawal record.
2. A parent requests a data export, then immediately requests a second one before the first completes → the second request either queues behind the first or is recognized as a duplicate-in-progress request (returning the existing request's status rather than spawning a redundant parallel export job) — implementation may choose either approach, but the parent must never see two simultaneously-conflicting "your export is ready" notifications for what should be one logical export.
3. An AI interaction occurs for a child whose family later requests full account deletion, and the 7-day grace period elapses → the AI Interaction History records for that family are subject to the same cascade-deletion/legal-retention rules as all other family data (cross-ref C.21's cascade worker), not independently retained beyond what's legally required.
4. A parent's AI Interaction History query spans a period with zero AI interactions (e.g., AI was disabled for that child the whole time) → shows an explicit "No AI interactions in this period" state, consistent with C.22's established empty-state pattern for the same conceptual absence.
5. A parent revokes a device that is, at that exact moment, in the middle of an active data-export-status poll from that same device → the in-flight read request may complete (read-only, low-risk), but any subsequent request from that revoked device fails authentication immediately after, consistent with C.23's established device-revocation timing pattern.
6. A parent changes the family-level language preference while a specific child has their own individually-overridden display language (per B.16) → the child's own override is unaffected; this screen's language picker only affects the family/parent-level default and any child without their own override.
7. A data export request is made for a family with a very large amount of historical data (long-tenured, many children) → the export job may take longer; the async status model already accommodates this via its "preparing" state, with no different handling needed beyond what the async design already provides.
8. A parent attempts to view AI Interaction History for a child whose AI has always been disabled (never enabled) → shows a friendly empty state distinct from "no interactions this period" — something like "AI has been off for this child the entire time," reinforcing that the absence is by configuration, not a missing-data issue worth flagging as suspicious.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Data export request fails to start (backend issue) | Clear retry option, never a silent failure |
| Duplicate export request while one is in-progress | Recognized and deduplicated, or queued; never two conflicting "ready" states |
| Consent withdrawal attempted on a required consent | Routed to the account-deletion explanation rather than a toggle action |
| PIN reset / device revocation failure | Standard C.19 error handling reused, no separate error path |
| Logout attempted with unsynced downloads | Confirmation prompt required before proceeding (FR-4) |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero AI interactions ever (AI always disabled) → distinct "AI has been off the entire time" framing (Edge Case 8).
- Zero AI interactions in a selected period (AI enabled but unused) → "No AI interactions in this period" framing (Edge Case 4).
- Zero data-export history yet → friendly "Request your first export anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Settings/Privacy screens: skeleton list shimmer for Consent Log, AI Interaction History, device list.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Settings screens render last-cached data offline; export requests, consent withdrawal, PIN reset, and device revocation all require connectivity and indicate this clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies entirely on the existing step-up authentication gate (C.19).

functional_requirements.requirement: Settings/Privacy & Support components (canonical, source NoorHeroes Blueprint Parent Settings screen): Security (PIN/biometric reset), devices list, consent log, AI controls per child (cross-ref/link only, configuration owned by C.23), language picker, export/delete account.

Settings actions: reset PIN, revoke device, review/withdraw consent, request export, request account deletion (cross-ref C.21 for the deletion flow itself — this screen's role is the entry point/link).

**Export and deletion require step-up authentication; deletion shows the 7-day grace period explicitly** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — restated; the deletion *experience* itself is C.21's, this screen only requires the same step-up before linking into it).

**Logout requires confirmation if any unsynced offline downloads exist** (source: screen catalog "Settings — Navigation Rules") — a data-loss-prevention courtesy check specific to the logout action on this screen.

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Navigation Rules") — the same `data_requests` record is queryable from both surfaces.

AI Interaction History entries are **redacted at write time, not just at read time** — `ai_interactions.input_redacted`/`output_redacted` are the only fields that ever exist for this data; there is no corresponding unredacted column anywhere in the schema for a later read-time filter to fail and leak (source §9.5 schema notes — a hard, structural guarantee, generalizing C.22's flags-only Safety Report into the fuller, still-safe, history view this screen offers).

Each AI Interaction History entry carries `model_version` and `policy_result` (e.g., allowed/blocked/redirected) alongside the redacted input/output summaries and an `expires_at` retention boundary — giving parents genuine context (what kind of interaction, what the system decided) without ever exposing a raw, re-identifiable transcript.

Consent Log entries are individually reviewable and, for optional consents (personalization, voice/AI, marketing — cross-ref A.1 FR-5's required-vs-optional distinction), individually withdrawable; **required consents (Terms, Privacy Policy, child-data-processing) cannot be withdrawn without triggering the broader account-deletion path**, since withdrawing a required consent is functionally equivalent to revoking the basis for the account's existence (cross-ref A.1's consent model, restated here as this screen's withdrawal-eligibility rule).

Withdrawing the AI/voice consent specifically here has the identical effect as toggling AI off via C.23's AI Permissions screen — this screen and C.23 read/write the **same** underlying settings field, never two independently-tracked values that could drift out of sync.

The language picker sets the app's display language; this is the same setting B.16's child-Profile language toggle exposes per-child — at the parent level, this screen sets the **default/family-level** language preference, distinct from (but consistent in mechanism with) a child's own individual override, if any.

PIN reset and device revocation on this screen reuse C.19's exact `ParentGateLauncher`/session-list mechanisms — this screen introduces no parallel PIN-storage or session-management implementation of its own.

Data export produces a structured, parent-readable export of the family's own data (consent history, child profiles' progress summaries, AI interaction history, billing history) — **never** including another family's data, and excluding raw biometric data (which never existed in exportable form to begin with, per A.1/C.19's zero-biometric-storage guarantee).

**Export and deletion require step-up authentication; deletion shows the 7-day grace period explicitly** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — restated; the deletion *experience* itself is C.21's, this screen only requires the same step-up before linking into it).

**Logout requires confirmation if any unsynced offline downloads exist** (source: screen catalog "Settings — Navigation Rules") — a data-loss-prevention courtesy check specific to the logout action on this screen.

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Navigation Rules") — the same `data_requests` record is queryable from both surfaces.

AI Interaction History entries are **redacted at write time, not just at read time** — `ai_interactions.input_redacted`/`output_redacted` are the only fields that ever exist for this data; there is no corresponding unredacted column anywhere in the schema for a later read-time filter to fail and leak (source §9.5 schema notes — a hard, structural guarantee, generalizing C.22's flags-only Safety Report into the fuller, still-safe, history view this screen offers).

Each AI Interaction History entry carries `model_version` and `policy_result` (e.g., allowed/blocked/redirected) alongside the redacted input/output summaries and an `expires_at` retention boundary — giving parents genuine context (what kind of interaction, what the system decided) without ever exposing a raw, re-identifiable transcript.

Consent Log entries are individually reviewable and, for optional consents (personalization, voice/AI, marketing — cross-ref A.1 FR-5's required-vs-optional distinction), individually withdrawable; **required consents (Terms, Privacy Policy, child-data-processing) cannot be withdrawn without triggering the broader account-deletion path**, since withdrawing a required consent is functionally equivalent to revoking the basis for the account's existence (cross-ref A.1's consent model, restated here as this screen's withdrawal-eligibility rule).

Withdrawing the AI/voice consent specifically here has the identical effect as toggling AI off via C.23's AI Permissions screen — this screen and C.23 read/write the **same** underlying settings field, never two independently-tracked values that could drift out of sync.

The language picker sets the app's display language; this is the same setting B.16's child-Profile language toggle exposes per-child — at the parent level, this screen sets the **default/family-level** language preference, distinct from (but consistent in mechanism with) a child's own individual override, if any.

PIN reset and device revocation on this screen reuse C.19's exact `ParentGateLauncher`/session-list mechanisms — this screen introduces no parallel PIN-storage or session-management implementation of its own.

Data export produces a structured, parent-readable export of the family's own data (consent history, child profiles' progress summaries, AI interaction history, billing history) — **never** including another family's data, and excluding raw biometric data (which never existed in exportable form to begin with, per A.1/C.19's zero-biometric-storage guarantee).

purpose: Give parents granular consent, safe AI-history, account security, language and asynchronous family data-rights controls. Screen-specific role: AI Interaction Detail (redacted).
edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent withdraws the marketing consent, then later wants to re-grant it (e.g., decides they do want promotional emails after all) → re-granting an optional consent is supported as a straightforward toggle-back-on action, creating a new consent-ledger entry (consistent with A.1's append-only, versioned consent-recording pattern) rather than attempting to "undelete" the prior withdrawal record.
2. A parent requests a data export, then immediately requests a second one before the first completes → the second request either queues behind the first or is recognized as a duplicate-in-progress request (returning the existing request's status rather than spawning a redundant parallel export job) — implementation may choose either approach, but the parent must never see two simultaneously-conflicting "your export is ready" notifications for what should be one logical export.
3. An AI interaction occurs for a child whose family later requests full account deletion, and the 7-day grace period elapses → the AI Interaction History records for that family are subject to the same cascade-deletion/legal-retention rules as all other family data (cross-ref C.21's cascade worker), not independently retained beyond what's legally required.
4. A parent's AI Interaction History query spans a period with zero AI interactions (e.g., AI was disabled for that child the whole time) → shows an explicit "No AI interactions in this period" state, consistent with C.22's established empty-state pattern for the same conceptual absence.
5. A parent revokes a device that is, at that exact moment, in the middle of an active data-export-status poll from that same device → the in-flight read request may complete (read-only, low-risk), but any subsequent request from that revoked device fails authentication immediately after, consistent with C.23's established device-revocation timing pattern.
6. A parent changes the family-level language preference while a specific child has their own individually-overridden display language (per B.16) → the child's own override is unaffected; this screen's language picker only affects the family/parent-level default and any child without their own override.
7. A data export request is made for a family with a very large amount of historical data (long-tenured, many children) → the export job may take longer; the async status model already accommodates this via its "preparing" state, with no different handling needed beyond what the async design already provides.
8. A parent attempts to view AI Interaction History for a child whose AI has always been disabled (never enabled) → shows a friendly empty state distinct from "no interactions this period" — something like "AI has been off for this child the entire time," reinforcing that the absence is by configuration, not a missing-data issue worth flagging as suspicious.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Data export request fails to start (backend issue) | Clear retry option, never a silent failure |
| Duplicate export request while one is in-progress | Recognized and deduplicated, or queued; never two conflicting "ready" states |
| Consent withdrawal attempted on a required consent | Routed to the account-deletion explanation rather than a toggle action |
| PIN reset / device revocation failure | Standard C.19 error handling reused, no separate error path |
| Logout attempted with unsynced downloads | Confirmation prompt required before proceeding (FR-4) |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero AI interactions ever (AI always disabled) → distinct "AI has been off the entire time" framing (Edge Case 8).
- Zero AI interactions in a selected period (AI enabled but unused) → "No AI interactions in this period" framing (Edge Case 4).
- Zero data-export history yet → friendly "Request your first export anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Settings/Privacy screens: skeleton list shimmer for Consent Log, AI Interaction History, device list.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Settings screens render last-cached data offline; export requests, consent withdrawal, PIN reset, and device revocation all require connectivity and indicate this clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies entirely on the existing step-up authentication gate (C.19).

Settings actions: reset PIN, revoke device, review/withdraw consent, request export, request account deletion (cross-ref C.21 for the deletion flow itself — this screen's role is the entry point/link).

**Export and deletion require step-up authentication; deletion shows the 7-day grace period explicitly** (source: screen catalog "Navigation Rules" — restated; the deletion *experience* itself is C.21's, this screen only requires the same step-up before linking into it).

**Logout requires confirmation if any unsynced offline downloads exist** (source: screen catalog "Settings — Navigation Rules") — a data-loss-prevention courtesy check specific to the logout action on this screen.

**Data-export requests are async; status shown here and in the web portal** (source: screen catalog "Privacy & Support — Navigation Rules") — the same `data_requests` record is queryable from both surfaces.

AI Interaction History entries are **redacted at write time, not just at read time** — `ai_interactions.input_redacted`/`output_redacted` are the only fields that ever exist for this data; there is no corresponding unredacted column anywhere in the schema for a later read-time filter to fail and leak (source §9.5 schema notes — a hard, structural guarantee, generalizing C.22's flags-only Safety Report into the fuller, still-safe, history view this screen offers).

Withdrawing the AI/voice consent specifically here has the identical effect as toggling AI off via C.23's AI Permissions screen — this screen and C.23 read/write the **same** underlying settings field, never two independently-tracked values that could drift out of sync.

The language picker sets the app's display language; this is the same setting B.16's child-Profile language toggle exposes per-child — at the parent level, this screen sets the **default/family-level** language preference, distinct from (but consistent in mechanism with) a child's own individual override, if any.

PIN reset and device revocation on this screen reuse C.19's exact `ParentGateLauncher`/session-list mechanisms — this screen introduces no parallel PIN-storage or session-management implementation of its own.

Data export produces a structured, parent-readable export of the family's own data (consent history, child profiles' progress summaries, AI interaction history, billing history) — **never** including another family's data, and excluding raw biometric data (which never existed in exportable form to begin with, per A.1/C.19's zero-biometric-storage guarantee).

edge_case_source:
### 1.10 Edge Cases

1. A parent withdraws the marketing consent, then later wants to re-grant it (e.g., decides they do want promotional emails after all) → re-granting an optional consent is supported as a straightforward toggle-back-on action, creating a new consent-ledger entry (consistent with A.1's append-only, versioned consent-recording pattern) rather than attempting to "undelete" the prior withdrawal record.
2. A parent requests a data export, then immediately requests a second one before the first completes → the second request either queues behind the first or is recognized as a duplicate-in-progress request (returning the existing request's status rather than spawning a redundant parallel export job) — implementation may choose either approach, but the parent must never see two simultaneously-conflicting "your export is ready" notifications for what should be one logical export.
3. An AI interaction occurs for a child whose family later requests full account deletion, and the 7-day grace period elapses → the AI Interaction History records for that family are subject to the same cascade-deletion/legal-retention rules as all other family data (cross-ref C.21's cascade worker), not independently retained beyond what's legally required.
4. A parent's AI Interaction History query spans a period with zero AI interactions (e.g., AI was disabled for that child the whole time) → shows an explicit "No AI interactions in this period" state, consistent with C.22's established empty-state pattern for the same conceptual absence.
5. A parent revokes a device that is, at that exact moment, in the middle of an active data-export-status poll from that same device → the in-flight read request may complete (read-only, low-risk), but any subsequent request from that revoked device fails authentication immediately after, consistent with C.23's established device-revocation timing pattern.
6. A parent changes the family-level language preference while a specific child has their own individually-overridden display language (per B.16) → the child's own override is unaffected; this screen's language picker only affects the family/parent-level default and any child without their own override.
7. A data export request is made for a family with a very large amount of historical data (long-tenured, many children) → the export job may take longer; the async status model already accommodates this via its "preparing" state, with no different handling needed beyond what the async design already provides.
8. A parent attempts to view AI Interaction History for a child whose AI has always been disabled (never enabled) → shows a friendly empty state distinct from "no interactions this period" — something like "AI has been off for this child the entire time," reinforcing that the absence is by configuration, not a missing-data issue worth flagging as suspicious.

### 1.11 Error Handling

| Scenario | System Behavior |
|---|---|
| Data export request fails to start (backend issue) | Clear retry option, never a silent failure |
| Duplicate export request while one is in-progress | Recognized and deduplicated, or queued; never two conflicting "ready" states |
| Consent withdrawal attempted on a required consent | Routed to the account-deletion explanation rather than a toggle action |
| PIN reset / device revocation failure | Standard C.19 error handling reused, no separate error path |
| Logout attempted with unsynced downloads | Confirmation prompt required before proceeding (FR-4) |

### 1.12 Empty States
- Zero AI interactions ever (AI always disabled) → distinct "AI has been off the entire time" framing (Edge Case 8).
- Zero AI interactions in a selected period (AI enabled but unused) → "No AI interactions in this period" framing (Edge Case 4).
- Zero data-export history yet → friendly "Request your first export anytime" framing.

### 1.13 Loading States
- Settings/Privacy screens: skeleton list shimmer for Consent Log, AI Interaction History, device list.

### 1.14 Offline States
- Settings screens render last-cached data offline; export requests, consent withdrawal, PIN reset, and device revocation all require connectivity and indicate this clearly if attempted offline.

### 1.15 Permission States
- No new runtime permissions; relies entirely on the existing step-up authentication gate (C.19).
